name: GREEN, the Hon. Nita Louise

headline.note: Green's pre-parliament work included an unidentified traineeship, retail and hospitality work, private legal practice at Maurice Blackburn, campaign, union and political-staff roles. Available sources do not establish complete employment boundaries, hours, leave or overlaps. Political staff, union work, campaign activity, study and elected office are excluded under the codebook; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Green's ALP biography says her first job after school was a traineeship, but does not identify the employer, occupation, dates, hours or employment conditions.
career_spells.counting_note: The employing sector, duration and substantive full-time status are unknown.

career_spells.role: Retail and hospitality work while studying
career_spells.evidence_note: The ALP biography records retail and hospitality work while Green studied. It supplies no employers, dates, hours, leave or evidence of continuity.
career_spells.counting_note: Unidentified work with unknown hours and dates cannot contribute to either headline.

career_spells.employer: University of Wollongong and University of Canberra
career_spells.role: Bachelor of Creative Arts and Juris Doctor student
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies identify the qualifications and institutions. Green's ALP biography links retail and hospitality work to her study, but none of the sources supplies enrolment or completion dates.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded from the employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies name Maurice Blackburn and the employment-law role. The ALP biography says Green was admitted as a Queensland solicitor in 2015 and then worked as an employment lawyer before becoming the Queensland field director for the 2017 Equality Campaign. The year boundaries express that sequence, not exact payroll dates; hours and leave remain unavailable. First speech thanks Peter Koutsoukis and Rod Hodgson for professional opportunity; useful historical firm leads, not dated employment evidence.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but exact boundaries and substantive full-time status are not sufficiently evidenced for a duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public biographies identify Green as Queensland Field Director for the successful 2017 marriage-equality campaign. The employing legal entity, payroll status, precise boundaries, hours and overlap with other work are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Campaign/nonprofit activity is excluded from the two employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies identify an AMWU industrial-officer or industrial-lawyer role, and the ALP biography says Green became an organiser after the 2017 Equality Campaign. A Queensland ministerial diary records Nita Green representing the AMWU at a meeting on 2 May 2018, establishing the role on that date. Exact appointment, cessation, hours, leave and overlap with political-staff work are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Union employment is excluded under the current headline method.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary and ministerial biographies identify Green as an adviser to Senator Murray Watt before her own Senate service. They do not publish the start date, end date, employing entity, hours, leave or overlap with the AMWU and election campaign. The 2019 end is bounded only by her commencement as a senator.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official sources record Green's Senate service from 1 July 2019.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded from the employment headlines.

research_notes: Follow up the unnamed traineeship and retail/hospitality employers, dates and hours, plus university enrolment and completion dates.
Obtain Maurice Blackburn appointment/cessation, full-time status and leave evidence; the 2015-2017 span records sourced sequence at year precision, not exact payroll boundaries.
Resolve whether the Equality Campaign role was paid employment and identify its legal employer, exact dates and overlap with legal practice.
Obtain AMWU appointment/cessation, title history, hours and leave and Senator Murray Watt adviser dates; reconcile their overlap with preselection and campaign activity.

2026-10-02 follow-up added three separately documented party offices and clarified first-speech locator: the saved debate starts with Sheldon but also contains Green later, so the URL itself was not wrong. Employer-specific Maurice Blackburn searches, Canberra/Wollongong study and traineeship/full-time searches found no reliable new boundaries or hours. LinkedIn profile open returned Internal Error and APH search reported robots restriction; official ministerial biography and accessible Hansard mirror used. US teacher/arts namesakes, staff job advertisements and another press-conference speaker’s mining traineeship were rejected as identity/context mismatches. Next leads: historical firm biographies via named supervising lawyers, university completion records, original traineeship employer, Equality Campaign/AMWU records and Watt office transitions. Exact hours remain unknown;2015 admission alone does not prove continuous2015–17 practice.
